title: Donald Trump Announces 2024 Presidential Campaign at Mar-a-Lago Under Cloud of Federal and State Probes
description_short: Donald Trump Announces 2024 Presidential Campaign at Mar-a-Lago Under Cloud of Federal and State Probes
description_medium: Donald Trump announced his 2024 presidential campaign at Mar-a-Lago on Nov. 15, 2022, one week after the midterm elections. The former president entered the race while facing several criminal and civil investigations. In his announcement speech, he pledged to return to the White House, formally beginning his campaign for another term.
description_long: Donald Trump announced his candidacy for the 2024 presidential election at his Mar-a-Lago estate on Nov. 15, 2022. The announcement came one week after the midterm elections, in which several candidates he backed lost, and while he faced multiple criminal and civil investigations. Trump used the speech to promise a return to the White House and open a campaign for a second, nonconsecutive term. The investigations formed part of the political setting around the announcement, but the information provided does not establish that the campaign launch was intended to influence any particular case. Nor does it identify a specific indictment that had already been brought at the time. The event began the 2024 campaign cycle for Trump and placed his political return alongside ongoing legal scrutiny.

title: Maine Secretary of State Removes Trump from Ballot
description_short: Maine Secretary of State Removes Trump from Ballot
description_medium: On December 28, 2023, Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows became the first state official to unilaterally remove a presidential candidate from the ballot, ruling Trump disqualified under the 14th Amendment insurrection clause. Bellows cited Trump role in the January 6 Capitol attack in her decision. Trump appealed. The ruling was stayed pending Supreme Court review. Combined with the Colorado ruling, the decisions forced the Supreme Court to definitively address whether January 6 constituted insurrection.

title: Supreme Court agrees to hear immunity case - Jan 6 trial delayed (Apr 22, 2024)
description_short: SCOTUS agreed to hear Trump's immunity appeal, effectively pausing the Jack Smith Jan 6 federal trial until after the election — a massive delay benefiting Trump politically.
description_medium: On April 22, 2024, the Supreme Court agreed to hear Donald Trump’s appeal arguing that a former president has immunity from prosecution in the federal Jan. 6 case. The decision paused the trial schedule until after the 2024 election, moving a major criminal proceeding past the campaign period.

title: Flood of Racist and Antisemitic Memes
description_short: Flood of Racist and Antisemitic Memes
description_medium: Throughout the fall of 2024, Donald Trump escalated his use of Truth Social to amplify racist, antisemitic, and white nationalist memes. He repeatedly 're-truthed' content from QAnon accounts and white supremacist users. This included AI-generated imagery and explicit dog whistles targeting minorities and political opponents, normalizing extreme fringe rhetoric in a mainstream presidential campaign.
